drawRectTooltip: Click and drag to draw a rectangle
helpStep1: Draw a selection: click the rectangle icon in the map toolbar (top-right) and drag to mark an area.
helpStep2: Set criteria: use the sliders to control minimum elevation, max slope, peak closeness, valley depth, and peak prominence.
helpStep3: Click "Analyze Area" — terrain data is fetched and analyzed entirely in your browser.
helpStep4: Explore results: directional markers show viewpoints on the map. Click a marker or result card for details.
helpStep5: Save favourites: use ❤️ Love or ⭐ Star buttons to bookmark spots across sessions.
helpStep6: Access warning: viewpoints may be near or on private property. Do not enter private land without permission, and stay on legal public access routes.
helpCreditsMap: Map data and basemaps are provided by OpenStreetMap, OpenTopoMap, and Esri.
helpCreditsGeocoding: Reverse geocoding is provided by OpenStreetMap contributors via Nominatim.
helpCreditsTerrainSources: Terrain sources include ArcticDEM, Geoscience Australia, Austria's DGM, Canada's CDEM, Copernicus EU-DEM, NOAA ETOPO1, INEGI, LINZ, Kartverket, the UK Environment Agency, and USGS 3DEP/GMTED2010/SRTM. Full source attribution: {{attribution}}.
helpCreditsIcons: Some UI icons are adapted from {{silk}} under {{license}}.

radioClickToBegin: Click on the map to place your transmitter. Right-click or long-press after that to set a direction target.
radioHelpTxAntennaGain: How much your TX antenna concentrates power forward, in dBi. Adds to TX power to give EIRP — it focuses energy, it doesn't create it.
radioTxGainUsePattern: Use typical gain from the selected pattern
radioHelpTxGainAuto: Auto-fills a typical gain when you change pattern. Turn off to type the exact gain printed on your antenna.
radioTxGainHintPattern: Using the typical gain for {{pattern}}: {{gain}} dBi. Uncheck above to type your own value.
radioTxGainHintNoTypical: No typical gain for this pattern. Enter the published or measured value if you have it.
radioTxGainHintCustom: Manual override. Enter the actual antenna gain.
radioHelpEngine: WASM is fast and the default. JavaScript is slower but useful as a sanity check.
radioHelpPolarization: How the wave is oriented. Match what your antenna actually transmits — vertical for most VHF/UHF, horizontal for HF and SSB beams. 45° slant is approximated as the average of the two.
radioHelpClimate: Regional atmosphere model. Pick what best matches your area; Continental Temperate is a safe inland default.
radioHelpSurfaceRefractivity: How strongly the lower atmosphere bends radio waves. 301 is a global average; raise it for humid coastal air, lower it for dry uplands.
radioHelpGroundType: Electrical properties of the soil along the path. Pick the type that best matches the route — sea water reaches farthest at low angles.
radioHelpGroundPermittivity: Custom ground only. Higher = wetter and more reflective.
radioHelpGroundConductivity: Custom ground only. Higher = more conductive (sea > wet soil > dry rock).
radioHelpStatMode: How strict the prediction should be. Median shows the typical signal; 90/90/90 shows what's reachable almost any time, anywhere, in any setup.
radioHelpStatTime: Percent of time the signal must hold. 50 = a typical day; 90 = nine days out of ten.
radioHelpStatLocation: Percent of spots within each cell that must work. Higher = also covers the less-favourable spots in the same cell.
radioHelpStatSituation: Percent of installations and clutter situations that must work. Higher = robust against unmodelled obstacles.
radioHelpMdvarBase: Which kind of link this is. Mobile fits car or handheld; Broadcast fits a fixed transmitter to many listeners.
radioHelpMdvarLocationModifier: Drops location randomness from the model. Leave off unless you're matching a specific NTIA scenario.
radioHelpMdvarSituationModifier: Drops situation randomness from the model. Same caveat — leave off unless you know you need it.
radioHelpResolution: Terrain detail level. Auto picks a reasonable balance; higher = sharper hills but more time and memory.
radioHelpRxHeight: Where the listener's antenna sits. Going from a handheld to a rooftop often does more than doubling TX power.
radioHelpRxGain: How much the receiving antenna boosts the incoming signal.
radioHelpRxSensitivity: The weakest signal the receiver can still decode. Lower (more negative) dBm = more sensitive radio.
radioHelpPatternPreset: Approximate horizontal shape of the antenna's radiation. For directional antennas, also set the pattern direction. Custom uploads a 360-line .az file.
radioHelpPatternDirection: Where the antenna points. 0° N, 90° E, 180° S, 270° W.
radioPatternMapHint: You can also drag the bearing handle on the map.
radioHelpSweepMode: Runs one wedge at a time. Slower, but lighter on memory and network.
radioHelpAdaptiveCulling: Skips obviously unreachable blocks before running ITM. Almost always safe to leave on.
radioHelpFastFill: Once a block looks uniformly strong, fills the rest without checking each cell. Turn off for a strict per-cell pass.
radioHelpPatternPreview: Polar plot of the current pattern, rotated to the bearing.
radioDirectionHint: After placing TX, right-click or long-press to set a direction target. The preview sector updates before analysis.
radioHelpAnalysisRadius: How far around the TX to compute. Bigger = slower and more memory.
radioHelpSectorAngle: Width of the wedge to analyze when you've set a direction. 360° covers all around.
radioTileLimitExceeded: Tile limit exceeded ({{n}} tiles). Try a smaller radius.
radioTileFetchFailed: Failed to load terrain tiles. Check your connection and try again.
radioWasmRequired: Radio Reach requires WebAssembly. Your browser may not support it, or the WASM module failed to load. Open the browser console for details.
radioLowFreqFallbackWarning: ITM is not valid below 20 MHz; results will use free-space approximation only.
radioClampedNotice: (capped at {{km}} km — max possible at this power/frequency)
radioMemoryGuardrail: This run is likely to exceed safe memory limits ({{mb}} MB total, {{bitmapMb}} MB bitmap, about {{ramGb}} GB RAM available). Reduce the area, use sweep mode, or lower the resolution.
radioMemoryWarningSummary: This run is estimated to use about {{totalMb}} MB total ({{bitmapMb}} MB bitmap, {{tileMb}} MB terrain/tile cache).
radioMemoryWarningRam: Detected available memory is about {{ramGb}} GB.
radioMemoryWarningSweep: Sweep mode is off, so the full coverage bitmap stays resident at once and large runs may crash the tab.
radioMemoryWarningManualZoom: A manual zoom was selected, so the auto downscaling guard is bypassed for this run.
